facts.F1: Story #6360 S03b Package Work Items, nwdes feature C of three (edge and rules). C1: Work Items no longer tells Flow metrics to update a Team's metrics: TeamDataService drops its teamMetricsService.UpdateTeamMetrics(team) call and a new Flow metrics reaction TeamDataRefreshedTeamMetricsUpdateHandler (Modules/FlowMetrics/Application/Policies) updates them when it hears TeamDataRefreshed, registered first among the TeamDataRefreshed handlers; an oracle first pins the event order and the handler-failure behaviour; if it shows a difference, fall back to D-2 e (ratchet only). C2: Work Items gets its own module rules (Domain reaches only the kernel and the BCL; Application in and out lists; Policies hold only domain-event handlers) with inline baselines compared both ways, measured from the IL; Flow metrics R4 loses TeamDataService; the two WorkItemService query edges stay named. C3: Work Items unit tests move to Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Modules/WorkItems/{Domain, Application, Application/Policies} (pure moves apart from edits) and WorkItemsUnitTestPlacementTest keeps them there; API/Integration tests stay. Behaviour-free for the user: routes, DTOs, refresh results, metrics answers, forecasts and the schema stay the same. Design: docs/feature/story-6360-s03b-package-work-items/feature-delta.md (D-2 a, D-8, D-9, slices C1-C3, Ratchet design 'New rules (C2)').

facts.F19: Claim-to-checker: the handler-order, success-path and accepted failure-path claims of one Team refresh pass are a finite state model, checked with Quint (quint run with a fixed seed for mutant counterexamples, quint verify with the Apalache backend at 12 steps, which covers a whole pass). No Agda, because no proof obligation over an unbounded domain exists. No TLC, because no liveness claim exists: a refresh pass is a finite sequence of awaited calls with no waiting, retry or scheduling, so eventual progress is not a claim of this change; refresh scheduling belongs to Epic 6474 slice 12. The dependency and placement claims of S1 to S3 are decided exactly by the compiled IL (IlDependencies over Mono.Cecil) and by test-file locations, each rule with a made-up offender as falsifier; they are not state claims. IlDependencies does not see catch-clause, event or attribute named-argument references; no edge of this change is of those kinds.
